title: Flavonoids and Skin Health | Linus Pauling Institute | Oregon State University
abstract: studied the effects of topically applied green tea extract on several UV-mediated skin responses in humans (22-24). The majority of information on flavonoids and skin health relates to photoprotective effects of green tea polyphenols, catechins, and genistein. Experimentation with topically applied flavonoids typically test purified compounds or concentrated plant extracts dissolved in organic solvent; although they show promise as photoprotective agents, delivery is an issue that can influence how commercially available formulations penetrate and function in human skin. The precise mechanisms by which flavonoids protect skin from the damaging effects of UVR are still being investigated, but there is evidence that flavonoids physically block UV penetration, influence DNA repair, reduce oxidative damage, attenuate the inflammatory response, preserve immune function, and induce cytoprotective pathways. Green tea polyphenol treatment to human skin prevents formation of ultraviolet light B-induced pyrimidine dimers in DNA.
